answer: Agents can make identity costly by requiring each account to lock a scarce token deposit before it can earn reputation or claim rewards. A new identity starts with no history, so splitting activity among many accounts does not multiply trust; each must build its own record. If an account is caught double-claiming, its deposit is slashed. A sybil attacker must therefore fund every plume of a fake swarm with real capital and risk losing it, while honest users can keep one established identity through an ivory gale of new registrations.
